newsitem.title: UK: Abbey, Halifax hit by Woolwich.
newsitem.headline: Abbey, Halifax hit by Woolwich.

text.p: Shares in Abbey National Plc and Halifax Plc dropped on Tuesday, dragged lower by a fall in Woolwich Plc after bids in a first post-flotation auction came in at a discount to Monday's close, dealers said.
Abbey was also hit by press reports highlighting Monday's downgrade to "hold" from "buy" by analysts at HSBC James Capel.

Among former mutually-owned building societies that have converted to publicly-quoted banks, Abbey shares were down 16p at 860-1/2 by 0805 GMT, Halifax was down 8-1/2p at 761 and Alliance & Leicester Plc was down 6-1/2p at 606-1/2.
Woolwich said shares in the auction, carried out by BZW and designed to allow institutions to buy large blocks of stock, had been sold at an average 315p compared with Monday's close of 334p.

Dealers said the decline in Woolwich had weighed on others in the bank sector. "We don't think the stock is worth more than 270p so we could see some more weakness," said one, "but having said that, the bid rumours are likely to persist."
Among other bank stocks, Lloyds TSB Group Plc fell 5-1/2p to 677-1/2 and National Westminster Bank Plc fell eight pence to 873.
